hints: Remember what Tollens' reagent actually tests for, and work backwards from that carbonyl type.
Hydrolysis replaces each Br with OH, so check which dibromide gives a gem-diol with both OH groups on carbon 1.
A gem-diol on a terminal carbon loses water to give an aldehyde, while a gem-diol in the middle gives a ketone that will not react with Tollens'.
walkthrough:
**Recall what gives a positive Tollens' test**

Tollens' reagent is oxidised by aldehydes only, not by ketones. So we need a hydrolysis product that can form an aldehyde.

Test result: $\text{R-CHO}$ gives silver mirror, $\text{R-CO-R'}$ does not

**Apply hydrolysis to the dibromides**

Complete hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH replaces each $\text{C-Br}$ with $\text{C-OH}$.

General rule: $$\text{R-Br + OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-OH + Br}^-$$

**Use the gem-diol rule**

If the two OH groups end up on the same carbon, water is lost to give $\text{C=O}$. A terminal gem-diol gives an aldehyde, an internal gem-diol gives a ketone.

Rule given: $$\text{R-CH(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{R-CHO + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check 1,1-dibromobutane**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHBr}_2$ hydrolyses to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}_2$. This is a terminal gem-diol, so it dehydrates.

Product: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO + H}_2\text{O}$$
This is butanal, an aldehyde, so Tollens' is positive.

options.A: 1,1-dibromobutane hydrolyses to butane-1,1-diol, CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)2. Loss of water gives butanal, CH3CH2CH2CHO. As an aldehyde it is oxidised by Tollens' reagent to give the silver mirror, so this is correct.
options.B: 1,2-dibromobutane hydrolyses to butane-1,2-diol, CH2(OH)CH(OH)CH2CH3. The OH groups are on different carbons, so no water is eliminated and no carbonyl is formed. No aldehyde means Tollens' is negative.
options.C: 1,3-dibromobutane hydrolyses to butane-1,3-diol, CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2(OH). Again the OH groups are separated, giving a stable diol with no C=O group. It cannot reduce Tollens' reagent.
options.D: 2,2-dibromobutane hydrolyses to butane-2,2-diol, CH3C(OH)2CH2CH3. Loss of water gives butan-2-one, CH3COCH2CH3. This is a ketone, and ketones resist oxidation so Tollens' stays negative. This is the classic aldehyde versus ketone trap.
